location_description: Carmel  is a suburban city in Indiana immediately north of Indianapolis. With a population of 100,777, the city spans 49 square miles (130 km2) across Clay Township in Hamilton County, Indiana, and is bordered by the White River to the east; the Hamilton-Boone county line to the west; 96th Street to the south and 146th Street to the north. Although Carmel was home to one of the first electronic automated traffic signals in the state, the city has constructed 141 roundabouts (as of September 2022) since 1998, earning its moniker as the "Roundabout Capital of the U.S."It is cited as one of the Best Places to Live in America by Money magazine and other surveys such as Wallet Hub, Niche, and SafeWise.
